rationale: C03 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the later letter. Both appoint a chairman to a temporary presidential policy commission concerned with a vital national resource, distinguish a broad long-range policy inquiry from narrower immediate problems, call for an objective and comprehensive review, prescribe a reporting deadline and enumerated subjects of study, and promise cooperation from interested parties. C22 and C04 contain closely related commission machinery, but C03 is the strongest match in the form, rhetoric, and sequence of a chairman-directed letter.

shared_material.child_excerpt: this Commission within the Executive Office of the President is to study the broader and longer range aspects of the nation's materials problem as distinct from the immediate defense needs
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Problems such as these cannot adequately be considered on a piecemeal basis. They must be viewed as parts of the broader problem of developing a total national communications policy
shared_material.explanation: Both define the commission's assignment as a broad policy review transcending narrower or immediate issues.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The task of the Commission, therefore, will be to make an objective inquiry into all major aspects of the problem ... and to make recommendations which will assist me in formulating a comprehensive policy
shared_material.parent_excerpt: An over-all, objective review of this entire situation is urgently needed ... a temporary Communications Policy Board ... to study and to make recommendations to me on the policies and practices which should be followed
shared_material.explanation: The distinctive objective-review, study-and-recommend framework is materially parallel.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am very pleased that you have agreed to serve as the Chairman ... I hope the Commission can report to me within the next six to nine months.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am asking you to serve as Chairman of this Board. In view of the need for early action ... I should like to receive the Board's final report by no later than October 31, 1950.
shared_material.explanation: Both letters appoint the addressee as chairman and immediately set a timetable for the final report.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I believe the Commission should study ... (1) The long-range requirements outlook. (2) The long-range supply outlook. (3) The prospect and estimated extent of shortages.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Order further states that the Board shall make recommendations ... concerning (a) policies for the most effective use of radio frequencies ... (b) policies with respect to international radio and wire communications, (c) the relationship of Government communications to non-government communications
shared_material.explanation: Each letter follows the general mandate with an enumerated set of specific inquiry areas adapted to the relevant resource.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Commission will enjoy the cooperation of all agencies of Government whose functions and interests relate to your assignment. And of course you will want to solicit the cooperation of private industry.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am sure that you will receive the full cooperation and assistance of all parties concerned.
shared_material.explanation: Both close the assignment by assuring broad cooperation, with the child elaborating the governmental and private sources of assistance.
